text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Deputy Finance Minister Peter Stanek said parliament should at least allow privatisation of the two largest commercial banks, VUB and IRB, while the largest insurer Slovenska Poistovna and the largest savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna could remain state-controlled.

- Stanek said privatisation of VUB and IRB could be carried out by selling off 10 to 15 percent stakes a year. This sell-off could be a test of privatisation for the two remaining state-contolled financial institutions, Sporitelna and Poistovna.

- The parliamentary opposition parties said they would again vote for the postponement of bank privatisation, while the ultra-left junior coalition member, the Workers Party (ZRS), said it could reconsider its current negative attitude to the bank sell-off.
- Hungarian-born financier George Soros delivers a lecture at the Slovak University of Economics on Wednesday.
PRAVDA - Transport Minister Alexander Rezes has offered his resignation for health reasons.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Finance Minister Sergej Kozlik said the government is preparing a law on collective investment which should create the legal framework for strategic investment in Slovakia.

- Swedish paper producer AssiDoman AB now owns about 91 percent of the Slovak paper and paperboard company JCP Sturovo. AssiDoman said it planned to buy the remaining nine percent in JCP from small individual shareholders.

SME - The Slovak parliament on Wednesday reopens an extraordinary session, interrupted last December, to debate direct presidential elections. Opposition parties said the assembly was unlikely to approve direct popular election of the president.
- President Michal Kovac is expected to announce the date for the referendum on the change to the presidential electoral system this week.
- Opposition parties said they would demand the dismissal of Minister of Culture, Ivan Hudec, for his "incompetent interference in the activities of cultural institutions.

- The Slovak Prognostic Bureau, a unit for economic analysis of the Academy of Science, said the current increase in wages did not threaten the country's economic development, as it is often presented by the government officials.
